question: A recruiter wants Claude to compare a set of candidate CVs against a job description. What is the most appropriate handling of the data?
options: A) Include everything and rely on the plan's privacy settings to protect the candidates' personal data.
B) Include the names but remove the skills, because a name on its own cannot identify anyone in practice.
C) Remove the names and contact details, keeping only the skills and experience the comparison needs.
D) Include the full CVs, since removing any details would make the comparison less accurate for hiring.
correct_answers: C) Remove the names and contact details, keeping only the skills and experience the comparison needs.
explanations: Plan settings are not a substitute for deciding what personal data needs to be there at all.
Names are identifiers, and removing the skills destroys the point of the comparison.
Correct. Data minimisation keeps the analysis useful while removing identifiers it does not require.
The comparison is against skills and experience, which survives removing identifiers.
